radiology_report:
Maastricht UMC+
Imaging Department
Date: 15 Jan 2025
Exam: mpMRI prostate

Clinical indication: PSA 9.0 ng/mL (rising trend from 4.3 ng/mL in Jun 2024), prior biopsy-proven prostate cancer, surveillance.

FINDINGS:
Prostate volume measures 58.0 mL.
T2-weighted imaging demonstrates a focal, ill-defined hypointense lesion within the right peripheral zone, approximately 14 mm in greatest dimension.
Diffusion-weighted imaging shows corresponding restricted diffusion with low ADC values.
Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences reveal early, intense enhancement of this same right-sided lesion.
No evidence of extracapsular extension, seminal vesicle invasion, or suspicious lymphadenopathy is seen.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS v2.1 score 4.
Prostate-specific antigen density 0.16 ng/mL/mL.
Clinical T stage cT1c.
csPCa predicted probability 0.86231947.

previous_notes.author: Dr. C. Peters (GP)
previous_notes.text: The patient presented for routine follow-up of his known prostate cancer diagnosis. PSA was 4.3 ng/mL, representing a significant rise from previous stable values. A decision was made to proceed with a repeat biopsy to assess for histological progression. The patient was referred to the urology outpatient clinic for the procedure.

pathology_report:
Biopsy timepoint 1 (18 Oct 2024):
Histological evaluation of the prostate tissue specimens reveals adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 3+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 2. The tumour is located in the right peripheral zone and demonstrates a cribriform and glomeruloid growth pattern. A cribriform pattern is present. There is no perineural invasion.

Summary:
The histological findings remain stable across the single documented biopsy timepoint, maintaining a Gleason 3+4 profile with high-risk architectural features.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 4.
